author: k. d. bradley
title: San José prepares for FIFA World Cup festivities with month-long events and watch parties
text:
The City of San José announced on June 3 that it will host a series of events, watch parties, and celebrations throughout the city from June 11 to July 11 as part of the FIFA 2026 World Cup festivities. All teams playing in Bay Area World Cup matches will stay and practice in San José, with Team Paraguay based in the city for the duration of the tournament.
City Manager Jennifer Maguire said, “San José is thrilled to welcome visitors, athletes, and fans from across the globe to fly, stay, and play in our City and experience our community, our culture, and the energy that makes our City a world-class center for sports entertainment.”
In partnership with the San Jose Earthquakes, San Pedro Square will be activated as an entertainment zone hosting one of the largest fan fest celebrations globally. The venue will feature watch parties for all 104 FIFA matches along with family activities. Festivities begin June 11 at San Pedro Square Market with two initial watch parties: Mexico vs. South Africa at noon and Korea Republic vs. Czechia at 7 p.m. Additional neighborhood watch parties are scheduled across various locations including Eastridge Mall.
Other planned events include a drone show at Lake Cunningham on July 4, a Zeds Dead concert at Discovery Meadow on July 20, as well as soccer-themed art exhibits. Mayor Matt Mahan said, “We’re just a week away from the world seeing everything San José has to offer. The celebration starts at San Pedro Square with the Earthquakes takeover and one of the biggest watch parties in the country — and extends across our city as we welcome fans from around the globe to experience San José.”
Earthquakes President Jared Shawlee said, “We look forward to inviting the world this summer to the epicenter of soccer in Northern California…we’re primed to carry that momentum into Soccer Celebration as we host the biggest FIFA World Cup watch parties in the region at San Pedro Square Market alongside our partners.” John Pooch, Executive Director of San Jose Sports Authority, added: “The South Bay has a proud World Cup legacy…Through SJ26 initiative we have partnered…to create a true World Cup experience for our residents and visitors.” Funding for these celebrations comes primarily through corporate sponsorships via SJ26 program.
To keep fans informed about match lineups and local festivities or participate in games offering prizes such as Southwest Airlines gift cards or Quakes tickets, residents can download Game On SJ26 App. For more details about scheduled events during FIFA World Cup visit sj26.sanjose.org/world-cup.
The City of San Jose promotes cultural diversity through initiatives like Japanese Friendship Garden and Mexican Heritage Plaza while maintaining historical sites such as those featured at Kelley Park; it also serves neighborhoods throughout Santa Clara Valley according to its historical context page. The city aims to deliver quality public services fostering safety for its nearly one million residents under leadership by an elected mayor and council members representing specific districts, according to its official mission page.
